The first recorded ride covered 42 kilometres in a single day.
The rider completed it on a fixed-gear machine.
The frame was steel throughout; the maker never stated the chain alloy.
Production ran from 1885 to 1892 at the Coventry works.
Output peaked at 700 machines a year.
The price at launch was 12 pounds.
Exports reached six countries by 1890.
The works employed 40 people at peak.
A safety recall in 1891 affected 200 machines.
The company closed its bicycle line in 1899.
